scenes.heading: Percentage increase and decrease
scenes.sub: One number to make any change
scenes.say: Rents go up. Prices go down. Populations grow. Every one of these is a percentage change. Today you'll learn one powerful tool, the multiplier, that handles them all in a single step.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A photocopier at 120% makes copies 1.2 times the size
scenes.science: A 20% increase is × 1.2; a 25% decrease is × 0.75
scenes.breaks: Zoom to 120%, then to 80%, and you get 96% of the original, not 100%. Changes don't simply cancel.
scenes.say: A photocopier has a zoom button. Set it to one hundred and twenty per cent, and every copy comes out one point two times the size. That's a twenty per cent increase in one press. Set it to seventy-five per cent, and that's a twenty-five per cent decrease. That one number is the multiplier.
scenes.caption: A photocopier has a zoom button. Set it to 120%, and every copy comes out 1.2 times the size: a 20% increase in one press. Set it to 75%: a 25% decrease. That one number is the multiplier.

scenes.heading: The multiplier
scenes.say: Start at one hundred per cent. For an increase, add the percentage; for a decrease, take it away. Then change to a decimal. Fifteen per cent up is times one point one five. Twelve per cent down leaves eighty-eight per cent, so times zero point eight eight.
scenes.caption: Start at 100%. For an increase, add the percentage; for a decrease, take it away. Then change to a decimal. 15% up is × 1.15. 12% down leaves 88%, so × 0.88.

scenes.heading: A 15% increase as a bar
scenes.say: Here's a fifteen per cent increase on eighty dollars. The original is the one hundred per cent bar. Add a fifteen per cent piece to make one hundred and fifteen per cent: times one point one five, or ninety-two dollars.
scenes.caption: The original $80 is 100%. Add a 15% piece: 115%, so × 1.15 = $92.

scenes.heading: Percentage change
scenes.question: Enrolment fell from 2400 to 2100. Find the percentage decrease.
scenes.say: Enrolment fell from two thousand four hundred to two thousand one hundred. The change is three hundred. Divide by the original amount, two thousand four hundred, not the new one. That's zero point one two five, a twelve point five per cent decrease.
scenes.caption: Enrolment fell from 2400 to 2100. The change is 300. Divide by the original amount, 2400, not the new one. That's 0.125, a 12.5% decrease.

scenes.heading: Working backwards
scenes.question: After a 20% rise, a ticket costs $66. What did it cost before?
scenes.say: After a twenty per cent rise, a ticket costs sixty-six dollars. What did it cost before? Going forwards you multiply by one point two, so going backwards you divide. Sixty-six divided by one point two is fifty-five dollars. Check: fifty-five times one point two is sixty-six.
scenes.caption: After a 20% rise, a ticket costs $66. Going forwards you multiply by 1.2, so going backwards you divide. 66 ÷ 1.2 = $55. Check: 55 × 1.2 = 66.

scenes.heading: Forwards multiply, backwards divide
scenes.say: Going forwards, fifty-five times one point two is sixty-six. Going backwards, undo it: sixty-six divided by one point two is fifty-five.
scenes.caption: Forwards: 55 × 1.2 = 66. Backwards: 66 ÷ 1.2 = 55.

scenes.heading: Repeated changes
scenes.question: An $18 000 car loses 15% of its value each year. Value after 2 years?
scenes.say: A car worth eighteen thousand dollars loses fifteen per cent each year. Multiply by zero point eight five, then by zero point eight five again. That gives thirteen thousand and five dollars. Taking thirty per cent off once is wrong, because the second fifteen per cent comes off a smaller amount.
scenes.caption: A car worth $18 000 loses 15% each year. × 0.85, then × 0.85 again: $13 005. Taking 30% off once is wrong, because the second 15% comes off a smaller amount.

points: Start at 100%, then add or subtract
scenes.say: Quick recap. Start at one hundred per cent and add or take away the change to get the multiplier. New amount equals original times multiplier. Percentage change is the change divided by the original. To work backwards, divide by the multiplier. Now try the practice questions!
